quiz.question: Where does service thirty return its clock value?

choices.text: In two thirty-two-bit halves in the argument registers.
As a file descriptor in the ordinary result register.
As an instruction count.

hints.text: Select the time service before executing syscall.
Treat the returned halves as bits of one value.

quiz.question: Why zero-extend the low half before OR?

choices.text: To change milliseconds into seconds.
To keep its sign extension from overwriting the high half.
To align the file buffer.

hints.text: Discard every bit above the low thirty-two bits.
Shift the high half into its final position before combining.

quiz.question: Which pointer may be byte-aligned rather than word-aligned?

choices.text: The native playback context.
The native display image.
The serialized file base.

hints.text: Keep the initialized failure status and zero accepted count.
Admit native alignment before native loads.

quiz.question: When is the actual required directory size known?

choices.text: After the file header supplies an admitted frame count.
Only after every frame has been displayed.
From the display address.

hints.text: Check pointer alignment and capacity as separate conditions.
Leave frame-count-dependent directory admission to the indexer.

quiz.question: Why rebuild validation state after reusing the file address?

choices.text: An address alone does not certify the bytes now stored there.
Native pointers change byte order automatically.
Every reload increases the frame count.

hints.text: Use the index context layout already defined in this chapter.
Private output fields can be initialized without publishing external results.

quiz.question: What does equal reload size establish by itself?

choices.text: That every CRC is correct.
That the byte counts agree; the contents still require validation.
That the old directory is safe to reuse.

hints.text: Pass the newly loaded count, not an earlier cached count.
Check the nested status before reading its successful output fields.

quiz.question: How many intervals remain when an eight-frame file starts at six?

choices.text: Six.
One.
Two.

hints.text: Treat the start as an unsigned frame index.
Admit it before requesting an anchor time.

quiz.question: Why use a seek for the first requested frame?

choices.text: To avoid validating the reloaded file.
To reconstruct the requested prediction state independently of old display pixels.
To skip the first interval.

hints.text: Populate every seek input from the admitted file or caller storage.
Keep the scratch image separate from the display.

quiz.question: Which sequence follows a successful seek to start six?

choices.text: Six.
Seven.
Zero.

hints.text: The first frame is supplied by seek, not by this record context.
Initialize private sequence state afresh for each playback.

quiz.question: Which work belongs inside this presentation schedule?

choices.text: The initial seek after the anchor.
The earlier file open and reload.
Every previous exercise in the chapter.

hints.text: Retain the anchor independently of the moving deadline.
Preserve the last observed time for backward-change checks.

quiz.question: Which value supplies the base for the next deadline?

choices.text: The latest actual clock sample.
The previous scheduled deadline.
The last encoded record size.

hints.text: Compare the unsigned sum with its original operand to detect wrap.
Check overflow before beginning that interval.

quiz.question: What must the next sequential delta use as its previous image?

choices.text: The old display from before the seek.
An all-zero image.
The successfully reconstructed start image.

hints.text: Use the caller's admitted display as the seek destination.
Do not repeat the seek for every following frame.

quiz.question: What should a later clock failure report about already accepted frames?

choices.text: That zero frames were accepted regardless of display changes.
That the entire display was restored.
The actual accepted count.

hints.text: Increment once per accepted logical frame, even when pixel values repeat.
Do not publish final external counters at this boundary.

quiz.question: What determines the remaining wait?

choices.text: The scheduled deadline minus the current admitted time, when positive.
The record payload length.
A fresh full duration after every decode.

hints.text: Read time after work rather than assuming decoding cost is zero.
Use the same clock-joining helper after every sleep.

quiz.question: How does this player handle a backward observed clock change?

choices.text: It silently starts a new schedule.
It fails while retaining the last accepted picture.
It sends a negative sleep request.

hints.text: Use unsigned ordering for the complete reconstructed value.
Admit monotonicity before treating a difference as a wait or lateness.

quiz.question: Why sample again after sleeping?

choices.text: Host sleep completion does not guarantee that the exact deadline was reached.
Every sleep changes the file's frame count.
The time service returns a record checksum.

hints.text: Request the difference only on the positive path.
Return to the sampling loop after service thirty-two.

quiz.question: How often can one interval increment the late counter?

choices.text: Once for every clock sample.
Once for every changed pixel.
At most once, when that interval completes late.

hints.text: Equality with the deadline is on time.
Compare lateness with the retained maximum using unsigned ordering.

quiz.question: What is the full logical duration of eight forty-millisecond display intervals?

choices.text: 280 milliseconds.
320 milliseconds.
Eight simulated instructions.

hints.text: Finish the interval before incrementing the index.
Leave anchor and scheduled deadline independent of actual lateness.

quiz.question: How is the final record window ended?

choices.text: At the exact accepted file count.
At the source image word count.
At the next allocated memory page.

hints.text: Use full-width address addition for the file base plus offset.
Do not read a directory entry beyond the final one.

quiz.question: Does an unchanged delta receive a display interval?

choices.text: No, because it has no changed pixels.
Yes, because it advances the logical frame sequence.
Only if it is encoded as full.

hints.text: Propagate nested status before advancing accepted progress.
Keep the private expected sequence across successive record calls.

quiz.question: When do the four final context outputs change?

choices.text: Only after every requested interval completes successfully.
Before validating the file.
Whenever a clock sample is read.

hints.text: Publish the four output fields together at the completed boundary.
Return the accepted count on both complete success and completed failure.
